title: Review of Systems Hub
examInfo: Two Canvas mock board exams of 200 questions each, INBDE style, with images and patient boxes. You get 200 minutes once you start.
Mock 1: Thursday, December 3. Mock 2: Thursday, December 10. Both 8:00 am to noon CST: start at 8:00 am, finish once you start; Canvas closes the exam at noon.
Remote, on Canvas with Respondus LockDown Browser and Monitor. Use a stable internet connection: the exams have images and patient boxes.
Pass/fail: complete the course's 8 quizzes and score 55% or better over the two mocks together (220 of 400).

Head & Neck Anatomy, Dental Anatomy & Occlusion, Fundamentals I and II, Oral Microbiology, Neuroscience, the systems courses (Cardio & Respiratory, Renal, Heme & Endo, MSK & GI), Ethics & Professionalism, Evidence-Based Dentistry, Radiology and Emergencies in the Dental Clinic.
The course hasn't said how many questions come from each course. This hub's mock spreads its 200 by the size of each course: a guess, not the exam's blueprint.
Self-study, November 16 to December 11, with no review sessions. Your earlier lecturers will answer questions if you ask them.

Each course is a section, cut into parts you can do in a sitting: high-yield notes, a Plain English version, a cram list and board-style questions. Built from the class's study guides, answered objectives and notes, the class above's, and this site's earlier hubs. Nothing from this course's quizzes.

likelyTopics.t: Horner syndrome: ptosis, miosis, anhidrosis and flushing from a cervical sympathetic lesion
Nerves at risk in thyroid surgery and the carotid sheath and its neighbors
Root of the neck: subclavian branches, phrenic nerve, thoracic duct and the superior thoracic aperture
Posterior triangle: CN XI and the cervical plexus at the nerve point
Suprahyoid and infrahyoid nerves, landmarks, carotid sinus and fascial spaces
Foramina of the skull and what passes through each (rotundum, ovale, spinosum, jugular foramen)
Cavernous sinus: contents, drainage and thrombosis with CN VI as the first sign
Cranial nerve lesions: III palsy, tongue and uvula deviation, UMN vs LMN facial weakness, corneal reflex
Epidural vs subdural vs subarachnoid bleeds
Visual pathway lesions and skull bones
Parotid: what runs through it, the duct opposite the maxillary second molar, IX–otic–auriculotemporal secretion, Frey syndrome
Facial nerve branches, Bell palsy and facial paralysis from a misplaced inferior alveolar block
Orbit: blow-out fracture, extraocular muscle actions and nerves, accommodation and glaucoma
Sensory supply of the face, scalp layers and lacrimal secretion
Muscles of mastication: actions, the lateral pterygoid as the opener, jaw deviation toward a V3 lesion
V3 branches, the chorda tympani on the lingual nerve, and the anatomy and complications of dental blocks
TMJ structure, compartments, dislocation and nerve supply
Maxillary artery parts and fossa boundaries
Pharyngeal arch nerves and derivatives, and pouch derivatives
Larynx: posterior cricoarytenoid as the only abductor, cricothyroid on the external laryngeal nerve, RLN injury, cricothyrotomy
Pharynx: all X except the stylopharyngeus, gag reflex, piriform recess and tonsillar bed
Clefts, tongue development and neck cysts
Ear: stapedius and hyperacusis, middle ear walls and the spread of infection
Fascial spaces and the mylohyoid line; Ludwig angina; canine space and the cavernous sinus
Tongue and palate nerves: V3 and chorda tympani in front, IX behind, X for the soft palate except the tensor veli palatini; palatal anesthesia
Pterygopalatine fossa openings and its ganglion
Maxillary sinus drainage and the teeth; nosebleeds and nasal drainage
Salivary glands and lymph drainage of the mouth
Converting between Universal, Palmer and FDI, permanent and primary
Eruption ages and sequences: primary central-lateral-first molar-canine-second molar; maxillary 6-1-2-4-5-3-7-8, mandibular 6-1-2-3-4-5-7-8
Primary versus permanent teeth, and the one-of-a-kind primary teeth
Calcification and root completion timelines; succedaneous teeth
Heights of contour on each surface, and what over- and undercontouring do
Canines: longest tooth, root and crown; maxillary versus mandibular canine features
Contact, embrasure and CEJ trends and their exceptions
Telling the incisors apart: maxillary lateral traits, mandibular central versus lateral, the cingulum
Molar roots and canals: palatal > MB > DB, MB2, the mesial root of mandibular molars, and the furcation levels
Premolar identification: maxillary first (two roots, mesial concavity), mandibular first (canine-like, marginal ridge), mandibular second (Y, H, U)
Maxillary molar crowns: cusp sizes, oblique ridge, Carabelli, lingual width; first versus second molar
Mandibular molars: five versus four cusps, grooves, smallest and tallest cusps
Fusion, gemination and concrescence (the tooth count), supernumerary and missing teeth
Hereditary versus acquired enamel and dentin defects: amelogenesis and dentinogenesis imperfecta, fluorosis, tetracycline, Turner tooth
Tooth identification, right or left included
Shape and root anomalies: taurodontism, enamel pearl, dilaceration, talon cusp, dens in dente, Hutchinson incisors
Attrition, abrasion, erosion and abfraction
Angle Class I, II (div 1 and 2) and III by the molar and canine relationships
Canine guidance versus group function, mutually protected occlusion, and which interferences are worst
CR versus MIP versus CO, and the CR-to-MIP slide
Determinants of occlusal morphology: what makes cusps taller or shorter, the horizontal determinants, fixed versus variable guidance
Centric and non-centric cusps, the curves of occlusion, freeway space
TMJ anatomy: the disc, the retrodiscal laminae, rotation vs translation compartments, and the ligaments' limits
Muscles of mandibular movement, especially lateral excursions
Posselt's envelope and the working and nonworking condyles
Articulators, the facebow and interocclusal records
TMD etiology and conservative care; occlusal trauma, mobility and wear
Globular protein classes (all α, all β, α/β, α+β), what stabilizes a fold, and the advantages of quaternary structure
Collagen: Gly-X-Y, the triple helix, vitamin C–dependent hydroxylation and the collagen diseases (scurvy, osteogenesis imperfecta)
Hemoglobin: cooperativity, T and R states, the Bohr effect, 2,3-BPG and fetal hemoglobin
Amino acid side chains (histidine's pKa) and the levels of protein structure
Carbohydrate isomers, glycosidic bonds, sucrose and S. mutans, GAGs and glycation
Lipid structure, base pairing and buffers
Potassium and excitability: hyperkalemia depolarizes (a mild rise nears threshold; enough locks Na+ channels inactivated), hypokalemia hyperpolarizes
The action potential: Na+ channel activation and inactivation gates, delayed-rectifier K+ channels, refractory periods and one-way conduction
Drugs and toxins on the action potential: local anesthetics (from inside, weak in acidic tissue), tetrodotoxin (Na+ channels, from outside) and TEA (K+ channels)
The neuromuscular junction: Ca2+ and the SNAREs, botulinum toxin, myasthenia gravis and acetylcholinesterase inhibitors
Resting potential: Nernst (a tenfold gradient = 60 mV), the K+ leak, and the pump-leak model (the pump adds little voltage)
Osmosis and tonicity: particles per molecule (NaCl 2, MgCl2 3, glucose 1), the reflection coefficient, swelling and shrinking
Transport mechanisms: passive, primary active (Na+/K+ ATPase) and Na+-driven secondary active transport; carrier properties
Synapses: electrical versus chemical, ionotropic versus metabotropic, EPSPs, IPSPs and summation, glutamate, GABA-A (Cl−) and glycine
Organelle functions and address tags, the cytoskeleton, and apoptosis
Modes of inheritance, pedigree clues and carrier risk (the 2/3 rule)
Oncogenes versus tumor suppressors (two hits), p53, RB, BRCA and HPV, inherited cancer syndromes, and benign versus malignant
Chargaff's rule, replication enzymes, leading and lagging strands, and telomerase
Transcription: σ and promoters, the lac operon, the three eukaryotic polymerases and epigenetic switches
RNA versus DNA, RNA processing and translation
Types of mutation, mutagens and the inherited diseases of the teeth
Enzyme definitions: catalytic power, specificity and regulation; the active site; cofactors, coenzymes, prosthetic groups, apoenzyme and holoenzyme; lock and key versus induced fit
How enzymes affect a reaction's thermodynamics: they lower ΔG‡ (the rate constant), never ΔG (the equilibrium constant)
Km, Vmax, the turnover number (kcat) and catalytic efficiency (kcat/Km)
Single- versus double-displacement (ping-pong) two-substrate reactions and their Lineweaver-Burk patterns
Thermodynamic systems, the three laws, enthalpy, entropy and Gibbs free energy (ΔG = ΔH − TΔS)
ATP: its free energy of hydrolysis, Mg2+, and energy coupling to the cell's three kinds of work
Steroid hormones: the three types and what they do, synthesis from cholesterol (mitochondrial P450 side-chain cleavage with NADPH and O2), carriers, intracellular receptors and the adrenal disorders
Enzyme inhibition on a Lineweaver-Burk plot: competitive, noncompetitive, uncompetitive and irreversible, with examples (malonate, lithium, penicillin)
Catabolic versus anabolic pathways, oxidation and reduction, NAD+ versus NADPH, and which tissues burn which fuel
Peptide versus steroid hormones, the second-messenger pathways and insulin
Rate-limiting enzymes and their regulators: PFK-1 and fructose 2,6-bisphosphate, isocitrate dehydrogenase, glycogen phosphorylase and synthase
ATP bookkeeping: 2 net from glycolysis, 3 NADH + 1 FADH2 + 1 GTP per turn, P/O ratios of 2.5 for NADH and 1.5 for FADH2, about 32 per glucose (30 with the glycerol 3-phosphate shuttle)
Electron transport chain and ATP synthase: proton pumping by complex, the binding-change model, cyanide at Complex IV, uncouplers make heat
Gluconeogenesis bypass enzymes, precursors and regulation; glucose 6-phosphatase only in liver and kidney (von Gierke disease when it is missing)
Glycogen synthesis and breakdown: glycogenin, branching and debranching, phosphorolysis
Pyruvate's fates and the PDH complex: lactate dehydrogenase, the five coenzymes, and regulation by phosphorylation
Complement: C3 is where the three pathways meet; what C3b, C3a, C5a and the MAC do; C1 inhibitor deficiency
Leukocyte extravasation: selectins, then integrins (LFA-1 on neutrophils binding ICAM-1), CXCL8, and the order cells enter
Pattern recognition receptors: TLRs, NLRs and inflammasomes, RLRs, CLRs; NF-κB drives the proinflammatory cytokines
How inflammation starts and resolves: sentinel macrophages, TNF-α and IL-1, prostaglandins and leukotrienes from arachidonic acid, M1 then M2 macrophages
Programmed cell death: apoptosis is silent; necrosis, necroptosis, pyroptosis and NETosis inflame
Innate cells and their jobs: neutrophils first, eosinophils, mast cells versus basophils, NK cells
Cell markers: CD34 hematopoietic stem cells, CD14 monocytes, CD11b macrophages, CD11c dendritic cells, CD16 and CD56 NK cells, CD19 and CD20 B cells, CD3 on every T cell
CD4 helper subsets as on the course chart (what induces each, what it secretes, what it does; FoxP3, TGF-β and IL-10 for Tregs) and the three signals of T-cell activation
MHC class I versus II and how each is loaded: proteasome and TAP for class I to CD8; endosome, invariant chain, CLIP and HLA-DM for class II to CD4
One B cell, one specificity: V(D)J recombination, RNA splicing for IgM with IgD, and class switching with CD40L and AID
Antibody isotypes: IgG crosses the placenta, IgM pentamer first, secretory IgA in saliva

Where each transporter and channel sits (apical or basolateral, which cell, which segment), and the exact segment and target of each diuretic
Apical and basolateral sides of every tubule cell: the Na+-K+-ATPase powers secondary active transport
Loop of Henle: water leaves the descending limb, not the ascending limbs; the corticopapillary gradient (about 600 mOsm/kg without ADH, 1,200 with it) and urea recycling

Collecting duct: several nephrons per duct; principal cells (ENaC, ROMK, aldosterone, ADH) and α- and β-intercalated cells

SIADH, central and nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, and ADH control
Reading a blood gas: the four simple disorders and their compensation

Hypoglycemia in the chair: the signs, the sulfonylurea or insulin with a skipped meal, oral glucose if awake, glucagon if not

Drug classes by mechanism and adverse effect: SGLT2 (yeast infections), GLP-1 (weight loss, C-cell warning), DPP-4, TZD (heart failure), the insulins
Type 1 vs type 2, C-peptide, HbA1c cutoffs and control before implants
Insulin release through the K-ATP channel, and diabetes in the mouth with its two-way periodontal link
hCG rescues the corpus luteum; what the placenta makes (not oxytocin); prolactin makes milk, oxytocin ejects it
Drugs that alter sex hormone signaling: GnRH analogs, 5α-reductase inhibitors, tamoxifen vs raloxifene, and thromboembolism
FSH and LH on Sertoli, Leydig, granulosa and theca cells; feedback; reading testosterone, LH and FSH; the LH surge
Male pathology: cryptorchidism, seminoma and the germ cell tumors, BPH (transition zone) vs prostate cancer (peripheral zone, Gleason)
HPV and cervical neoplasia at the transformation zone; endometrioid vs serous endometrial carcinoma; pregnancy gingivitis and pyogenic granuloma

Classifying the leukemias (acute vs chronic, myeloid vs lymphoid): AML with Auer rods, ALL in children, CML with t(9;22) and imatinib, CLL with smudge cells, APL
Hodgkin vs non-Hodgkin, and the lymphomas with associations: Burkitt t(8;14), MALT with Sjögren, myeloma's CRAB

Portal-caval anastomoses in portal hypertension (esophageal varices, caput medusae, rectal varices) and the portal vein lying in front of the IVC
Midgut and hindgut arteries: the pancreaticoduodenal (celiac–SMA) and marginal (SMA–IMA) anastomoses and the splenic flexure watershed

Viral hepatitis A–E: spread, chronicity, hepatitis B serology and hepatitis C's oral lichen planus link, with infection control
Acid drugs (PPIs vs H2 blockers, antacid chelation) and peptic ulcer disease (H. pylori, NSAIDs)
Crohn disease vs ulcerative colitis and celiac disease, their oral findings, and the IBD drugs
Antiemetics and their side effects (extrapyramidal effects, neuroleptic malignant syndrome, long QT) and antidiarrheals
GERD's dental erosion and Barrett esophagus, and how colorectal cancer presents
Bone drugs and MRONJ: bisphosphonate mechanism, denosumab, teriparatide (no MRONJ), and who is at highest risk
Bone disorders with oral signs: osteogenesis imperfecta, achondroplasia (FGFR3), osteopetrosis, cleidocranial dysplasia, Paget disease
Osteoclast biology: RANKL, OPG and M-CSF, and PTH acting through osteoblasts
Intramembranous vs endochondral ossification; cartilage types and collagen types
Calcium balance: hypocalcemia after thyroid surgery and the osteoporosis risk factors
OA vs RA (pannus, Heberden and Bouchard nodes, RF and anti-CCP, the TMJ) and gout (urate needles, first MTP, allopurinol)
Sjögren syndrome (the most dentally relevant), lupus antibodies, scleroderma in the mouth, Graves vs Hashimoto
Nutrient function and deficiency: thiamine, vitamin C, folate vs B12, kwashiorkor edema
Bone tumors by age and site: metastases first, osteosarcoma, osteoid osteoma, giant cell tumor, Ewing sarcoma
HLA-B27 and the seronegative spondyloarthropathies
Pemphigus vs pemphigoid (desmosome vs hemidesmosome, intra- vs subepidermal, Nikolsky), dermatitis herpetiformis and lichen planus
Basal cell vs squamous cell carcinoma vs melanoma (ABCDE, Breslow thickness)
Dermatologic drugs: absorption, steroids vs calcineurin inhibitors, isotretinoin, permethrin, antifungals
Excitation-contraction coupling, troponin C, ATP in the cross-bridge cycle, sarcomere bands
Succinylcholine (pseudocholinesterase, malignant hyperthermia), reversal with neostigmine or sugammadex, spasmolytics
The five principles in Code order and naming the principle a scenario turns on
Colleagues: justifiable criticism of prior work and the impaired colleague
Veracity and fees: amalgam removal, copayment waivers and overbilling, split fees, advertising and product sales
Records, abandonment, emergencies, abuse reporting, postexposure duties and patients with HIV or hepatitis
Informed consent and refusal: what to disclose, Canterbury's reasonable-patient standard, capacity and consent for minors
Bloodborne pathogens: transmission risks, the steps after a needlestick, and OSHA's hepatitis B vaccine rule
Confidentiality, HIPAA and the duty to warn
Arguments, fallacies and moral theories
Reporting suspected child abuse and neglect
Efficacy versus effectiveness, the study-context continuum and the three evidence-to-practice gaps
Pre-appraised evidence: literature review, systematic review, meta-analysis and guideline; the pyramid; GRADE and AGREE
Naming the design from a study description, and what case-control and cohort studies are each good for
The 5 A's in order and building a PICO(T) question; question types and their best designs
Sensitivity, specificity and predictive values: calculating them and choosing a test for screening or confirming
Reading relative risk, odds ratio, hazard ratio and NNT with their confidence intervals and p-values; type I and II errors and power
Internal and external validity; bias, confounding and chance; randomization, blinding and intention-to-treat
Standardization, calibration and reliability; precision versus accuracy
Photoelectric absorption as the source of contrast (∝ Z³, bone ~6.5× soft tissue)
mA/time (quantity) versus kVp (quality/penetration), and filtration
Bremsstrahlung as the primary source of x-rays; >99% heat vs ~1% x-rays
Beam attenuation shares (Compton ~57%, photoelectric ~27%, coherent ~7%) and the inverse square law
Deterministic (threshold, dose-severity) versus stochastic (no threshold) effects with examples
Direct versus indirect action and the DNA double-strand break
ALARA and the three protection principles; rectangular collimation, thyroid collar, 1 mSv dosimeter
Radiosensitivity by cell/organ (fast-dividing most sensitive)
Vertical-angle errors: excessive = foreshortening, deficient = elongation
Paralleling versus bisecting angle and the four rules of projection geometry
Error-cause pairings: overlap, cone cut, missing crown, blur; XCP color coding
Maxillary radiopaque landmarks: anterior nasal spine, zygomatic process (J/U), Y line of Ennis
Lamina dura, the mental foramen mimic, and the egg-shell effect
Panoramic focal trough, ghost images and positioning errors
Basic life support in the office: C-A-B, the 10-second breathing and pulse check, compressions, the AED
The emergency kit: each drug's use, dose, route and catch (epinephrine, nitroglycerin, aspirin, naloxone, diphenhydramine, albuterol)
Prevention: the history, putting off elective care after an MI, never stopping blood thinners yourself, "clearance"
Head tilt-chin lift and the genioglossus
Foreign-body aspiration: mild versus severe, abdominal thrusts, no blind finger sweep, right main bronchus, ER for X-rays
Mallampati classes and the difficult airway
Laryngospasm in the lightly sedated patient
Anaphylaxis: IM epinephrine in the thigh first
The surgical airway: cricothyrotomy
Chest pain: oxygen, nitroglycerin and its contraindications, chewed aspirin, 911
Endocarditis prophylaxis: who needs it, which procedures, amoxicillin 2 g and the allergy options
Bleeding: pressure first, local measures, and blood thinners left to the prescriber
Hypertensive urgency versus emergency
Hypoglycemia: the numbers, juice versus glucagon versus IV dextrose
Rule of twos and adrenal crisis (hydrocortisone 100 mg)
Vasovagal syncope: prodrome, legs up, recovery
Local anesthetic overdose: maximum dose, signs, IV lipid emulsion
